data.narrative:
Stratum AI is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Daniel Mogilny and Farzi Yusufali. The Climate & Energy sector comprises 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Lonza), though seed-stage peers within this cohort are sparse. With $400K in total raised, Stratum occupies an early position in a capital-intensive sector where later-stage comparables include Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach given insufficient density of same-stage or adjacent-stage peers to support peer-median analysis. Using total raised as a proxy base value of $400K and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $1M. This reflects the expected expansion in enterprise value between capital raises in early-stage venture, absent more granular peer benchmarking.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $850K to $1.15M, centered at $1M. Key uncertainties include the absence of near-peer seed-stage transactions in Climate & Energy—the sector's capital intensity and technical risk profile may drive valuation inflection points not visible in stage-based mechanics alone. Additional validation would require either identified seed-stage Climate & Energy comparables or bottom-up traction metrics from Stratum itself. The single-method foundation warrants conservative weighting pending further diligence.
